01 Brand Strategy

Eliminate campus transit friction.

Gbera exists because getting from Bello Hall to a 9am class shouldn't require a negotiation. The brand is built to feel fast, locally grounded, and seamlessly modern — reliable tech utility with the pulse of student culture running through it.

Mission

Move students without friction.

Fast, structured, transparent mobility built for the rhythms of campus life — lectures, exams, late-night library runs.

Vision

The default movement engine.

To turn chaotic, informal keke commutes into a seamless, shared experience that every student defaults to.

Positioning

Built for campus, not adapted to it.

Not a shrunk-down city ride-hailing app. Gbera is designed from the ground up around hostels, faculties, and gates.

V  Core Values

Velocity

Fast matching, quick pickups, no lag between tapping "book" and seeing a keke move toward you.

Community

Built for students, driven by local landmarks — Kuti Hall, the Zoo, Mellanby — not generic map pins.

Clarity

Flat, transparent pricing and straightforward navigation. No surge, no surprise, no small print.

02 Logo & Mark

A pin, taking off.

The mark reads as a map pin — an outlined ring in Gbera Yellow — with a black chevron launching forward through it, mid-motion. It is legible at app-icon size and holds up at wall scale without losing intent.

Primary lockup — full color on light ground

  • Pin ringAn open circular ring in Gbera Yellow stands in for the map-pin silhouette — a location marker rendered as a loop rather than a filled teardrop, so it reads as a place you're leaving, not one you're stuck at.
  • Forward arrowA solid black chevron launches through the ring's opening, angled up and to the right — the "taking off" moment the name Gbera describes, caught mid-departure.
  • Negative spaceThe arrow is cut from solid black with no outline, so it reads cleanly against yellow, white, or Cloud Gray. It has no built-in contrast against dark grounds — see Logo on Color below.
  • Lowercase logotypeSet in Space Grotesk Bold, sitting directly beneath the mark at matching optical width — never stretched, condensed, or set in a different weight.

Lockups

Full color — primary usage

Mark only — app icon, favicon, avatar

Mark on Gbera Yellow — social & app tiles

Logo on color

The mark is built for light and mid-tone grounds — white, Cloud Gray, and Gbera Yellow. The ring keeps its yellow fill on white and gray; on a yellow ground, the ring recedes and only the black arrow reads, which is intentional restraint, not a broken lockup.

✓ On white / Cloud Gray

✓ On Gbera Yellow (arrow only reads)

✕ On Asphalt Black — arrow disappears. Use the wordmark alone in Cloud Gray instead.

Clear space & minimum size

Maintain clear space on all sides equal to the height of the arrow's vertical span (marked x). Never let text, edges, or other UI elements enter this zone.

Digital minimum: 24px for the mark alone (app icon / favicon). Print minimum: 12mm width for the standalone mark; the full lockup should not run narrower than 30mm.

Misuse

DON'T

Flip or mirror the mark's direction

DON'T

Recolor the mark off-palette

DON'T

Stretch or distort the proportions

DON'T

Place on low-contrast dark backgrounds

Balance of use

Yellow leads, but it is not the default fill — it is reserved for moments of action. Most surfaces stay quiet in Cloud Gray and Asphalt Black so that yellow keeps its charge.

04 Typography

Legible under pressure.

Students read this app while running to Kuti Hall for an exam. Both typefaces are geometric, upright, and built to hold up at speed — one carries the brand's voice, the other carries the interface.

Space GroteskBold 700 — logo, headlines, marketing
Your campus. Your pace.
InterRegular 400 / Medium 500 — UI, body, pricing
Where on campus? Finding your ride — your Gbera is three minutes out.

Type scale

DisplayGrotesk 700 / 56pxGbera
H1Grotesk 700 / 32pxBook a ride
H2Grotesk 600 / 22pxShared or Exclusive
BodyInter 400 / 16pxFlat rate, no surge, no surprise fees.
UI LabelInter 600 / 13pxBello Hall
CaptionInter 500 / 11pxEstimated arrival: 4 min

Pairing rule

Space Grotesk never appears in body copy longer than a headline or a single UI label — its geometric quirks (the flat-topped "a", the squared curves) slow down long reading. Inter carries every sentence longer than a tagline, including all pricing and driver information.

03 — Ride type selection

Splash A 3–5 second high-impact load on solid Gbera Yellow. The mark pulses forward once before transitioning into the map — one deliberate motion, not a loop.

Map Custom layering mutes roads to Cloud Gray and elevates campus landmarks as interactive nodes — Bello Hall reads before "junction 4" ever would.

Ride types Shared shows passenger silhouettes on a standard line; Exclusive Drop gets a single rider icon and a glowing yellow direct route.

07 Campus Merchandise

Lifestyle streetwear, not promo swag.

Physical presence is how Gbera earns campus adoption before the app ever gets opened. Every piece should look like something a student chose to wear, not something handed out at a stand.

Graphic Tee — Front

Heavyweight cotton, Asphalt Black. Minimalist "Gbera." logotype centred across the chest — no mark, letting the wordmark carry the piece.

Graphic Tee — Back

A stylised, retro-tech wireframe of a tricycle wheel with "Movement Engine" set beneath it — the one place the brand allows a technical, blueprint feel.

Laptop Stickers — Mark

Die-cut vector stickers of the standalone mark in rotating brand colourways for laptops that already have a lid full of stickers.

"I survived the
Bello Hall trek."

Laptop Stickers — Inside Jokes

Localised campus humour that only a UI student would clock — this is where the brand's community value shows up as physical, shareable proof.
